description: We are VYRON , a team of passionate college students interested in technology, space exploration, and innovation.
summary: One interactive map of Mars that fuses data from multiple NASA missions so a human crew can plan a Marswalk — where to walk, what science to do, and what hazards to avoid. Martian Map layers 11 real mission sites onto the Celestia Mars shaded mosaic, with toggleable water-ice and dust-storm planning zones, and a click-to-plan route tool that draws a traverse, measures its distance, and estimates EVA time. One click loads a verified sample Marswalk from Jezero Crater to Nili Fossae: 234.0 km in about 67.9 hours of estimated EVA time.
details:
The first astronauts on Mars will need the best map possible: where to walk, what science to do along the way, and what hazards to avoid — all in one view. Today that information lives scattered across mission datasets, rover traverse maps and separate science papers. VYRON's Martian Map is a layered, interactive map that brings it together: Real Mars basemap — Celestia Mars shaded global mosaic via OpenPlanetaryMap, for terrain reading. 11 real sites with mission data — Jezero (Perseverance), Gale (Curiosity), Elysium (InSight), Gusev (Spirit), Meridiani (Opportunity), Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, Eberswalde, Hellas Planitia, the Phoenix site, and Nili Fossae. Each carries its mission, key findings and a Marswalk science objective. Click-to-plan routes — click the map to add waypoints; the app draws the traverse, computes leg and total distances using Mars' mean radius (3,389.5 km), and estimates EVA time (~3.5 km/h plus 30 min per science stop). Hazard and resource layers — toggleable, clearly labelled approximate zones for water-ice candidates (Mars Odyssey hydrogen data) and dust-storm source regions, so route choices weigh risk against science value. One-click sample Marswalk — Jezero Crater to Nili Fossae, verified 24 Oct 2026 at 234.0 km and ~67.9 h estimated EVA, with a copyable text itinerary ready to paste into a field plan. Built as a single self-contained web page with Leaflet and JavaScript, so the whole tool runs from one public link with no install. Its creative step is fusing four kinds of data — optical imagery, topography, hydrogen/water-ice signals and dust climatology — into one planning view, and every figure is reproducible from the stated method: Mars mean radius 3,389.5 km, about 3.5 km/h plus 30 minutes per science stop.

SI disclosure: the AI assistant Muse helped write the app code, draft this text and build the demo deck; the deck's Mars images are SI-generated illustrations, captioned as such.
